question:
An LED material has band gap $E_g=1.95\,\text{eV}$. The same p\text{–}n junction is used as a reverse-biased photodiode. Assume it produces a detectable photocurrent only if the incident photon energy satisfies $E_{ph}\ge E_g$ (sharp threshold).

Two monochromatic hydrogen Balmer photons are incident separately on the photodiode:

(i) $3\to2$ transition (H$\alpha$ line)

(ii) $4\to2$ transition (H$\beta$ line)

Use $E_n=-\dfrac{13.6}{n^2}\,\text{eV}$. Calculate the photon energies $E_{32}$ and $E_{42}$ and determine which of the two photons will be detected. Show the comparison with $E_g$ and state the final conclusion clearly.
